title: Assistant Wizardry Playbook — guided playground scratchpad
content:
Quick context (noisy personal notes)

Goal: sketch a lightweight, non-dev-friendly guided playground inside the Console and as an embeddable widget. Help PMs, designers, and internal CS reps craft and test prompts and response-mode presets without needing to write code.

Why: lots of customer feedback that product managers want to prototype assistant behaviors quickly; solutions-engineering gets repeated requests for small tweaks. Right now prototyping requires SDK usage or ad-hoc scripts.

Core idea: a multi-step wizard that lets a user (1) pick an intent or scenario, (2) select persona/response mode (concise/expanded/citation-aware), (3) choose cost envelope (economy/standard/premium), (4) bind example user messages and constraints, (5) iterate with live responses and diffing across model variants.

Target surfaces
- Console: guided tab under hosted-api -> Playground (first-class)
- Embeddable iframe / React component for internal demos or partner sandboxes
- Quick-export: copy SDK snippet or save as a route preset

User stories (rough)
- As a PM, I want a template for "customer support reply assistant" so I can prototype tone + length and export a working route to share with eng.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to run A/B across two model variants and see per-response cost delta and latency, so I can recommend a rollout plan.
- As a designer, I want to toggle persona attributes (friendly/formal) and view sample turns in a left/right pane for quick sign-off.

Feature checklist (MVP slice)
- Templates: 6 starter scenarios (support, search-assistant, sales-suggester, code helper, summarizer, meeting-recap) — quick copy/edit
- Persona toggles: tone (formal/casual), verbosity (short/medium/long), safety strictness (strict/normal/lenient)
- Cost slider: sets token budget and picks model variant bucket (cheapest, balanced, fidelity) — show estimated per-call cost and latency band
- Live run: single-turn + multi-turn replay (history up to 12 turns), streaming enabled
- Compare mode: side-by-side runs with different configs; show token count, estimated cost, latency, top-3 differences in output (diff/view)
- Save/export: save as preset (console route) or export SDK snippet (python/js)

Nice-to-have (later)
- Behavioral eval harness: run a small eval set (10 prompts) and surface basic pass/fail metrics (toxicity checks, hallucination heuristics)
- Integrations: link to customer conversation samples (redacted) for "run against my corpus"
- Shareable links with read-only playback for stakeholders

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Non-dev user can create/edit template and run at least 1 comparative test without SDKs
- Exported preset generates a route config file that eng can use to create a canary (internal format TBD)
- UI surfaces estimated per-call cost, token counts, and latency band for each run
- Basic telemetry sent: template used, runs per user, A/B usage, conversions -> saved preset / exported SDK

Operational considerations / infra notes
- Backend: reuse existing hosted-playground inference routing but add a thin orchestration layer for parallel comparative runs. Need safe quotas for sandbox accounts.
- Billing: sandbox runs should be flagged and excluded from billing metrics unless explicitly saved/exported with 'production' toggle.
- Security: example corpus upload must auto-redact PII and require confirmation + retention TTL.
- Data residency: iframe embeds should respect org-level region preferences.

Open questions / TODOs
- What are the exact model buckets we expose? (open-llm-lite | balanced-xx | high-fidelity) -> sync with model-catalog team
- How to represent "cost slider" mapping to actual runtime quantization/packing settings for Dedicated/Private customers? Might need a hint/preview only for non-dedicated accounts.
- UX: should compare-mode show diffs in-line or side-by-side with highlights? prototype both.
- Team ownership: short-term - devexp + hosted-api; long-term - partner with optimize for eval hooks.

Quick tech sketch (very rough)
- Frontend: React (console common components) + small state machine for wizard steps
- Backend: playground orchestrator service (stateless) that fans out parallel requests to the runtime, aggregates token counts and latencies, returns structured meta + outputs
- Storage: presets saved to user-profile namespace; export blob (yaml/json) includes prompt templates, persona settings, cost envelope, and chosen model id

Risks / failure modes
- Users mistake sandbox results for production performance -> need clear banner and produced example of production vs sandbox differences
- Cost surprises if UI misrepresents real-world token usage -> show conservative estimates and raw token counts after run
- Privacy issues when using customer-conversations upload -> require two-step confirmation and purge policy

Immediate next steps (notes to self)
- Sketch 3 wireframes: a) single-run flow, b) compare-mode flow, c) save/export modal (deadline: EOD next week)
- Quick sync with model-catalog (Mika) to define 3 model buckets and estimated cost mapping
- Draft telemetry event definitions with analytics (Priya)
- Put PRD skeleton into Confluence (link: CONFLUENCE-1234) and create Jira epic JIRA-PLAT-987

Random brainstorming fragments (keep)
- "Persona tokens" — allow attaching a small JSONL file of example turns to bias persona during runs
- "Cost badges" — little UI chips that say: < 5c | ~10-20 token median | <100ms typical (fake numbers)
- "Run recipes" — community-shared presets gallery (internal first)

Notes-to-self: write a short demo script for the next all-hands — show a PM building a support assistant in under 7 minutes. Capture analytics to show time-to-prototype improvements.

-- end of rough scratchpad (messy, apologies)
